title: Mexico Turns to China as U.S. Threats Mount – Soberanía 123
author: Mexico Solidarity
content:
In episode 123 of Soberanía, hosts José Luis Granados Ceja and Kurt Hackbarth
cover Mexico's foreign minister Roberto Velasco's visit to China, where
Beijing reaffirmed its support for Mexico's sovereignty and opposition to
foreign interference — a clear signal as Mexico seeks to diversify its
relationships amid U.S. pressure. The hosts argue that with the U.S.-Canada
trade war escalating (including unprecedented product bans), Mexico cannot
afford to remain dependent on a single partner, especially as the U.S.
declines technologically while China leads.

Next, they break down the 2027 economic package, which avoids raising taxes on
the wealthy and instead targets tax evasion through fake invoicing (the
"factureras") and pushes for a digital economy with reduced cash use. While
the hosts support going after tax cheats, they question the plan's reliance on
private banks — which charge exorbitant fees — instead of strengthening the
state-run Banco de Bienestar. They also highlight the real culprit behind weak
investment: Trump's instability, not Mexico's policies, and note that foreign
direct investment remains at record highs.

The episode then examines a suspicious document published by Televisa's
investigative unit, allegedly showing Senator Julieta Ramírez seeking a
cooperation deal with the U.S. Justice Department. The hosts point out
multiple red flags: the document is in Spanish without an accompanying English
version, has no signatures, and Televisa didn't contact Ramírez or the DOJ for
comment. They suspect either journalistic incompetence or a deliberate smear
against a rising Morena politician from a border state.

Losers and Haters takes aim at Fox News for hyping the Pentagon's downing of
"cartel drones" as a justification for lethal military action — when Mexican
officials have clarified these are commercial surveillance drones used for
migrant trafficking, not weapons. The hosts see this as part of a deliberate
campaign to build public support for unilateral U.S. military strikes in
Mexico.
